title: Communicate a difficult truth accurately and respectfully

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Honesty includes relevant omissions and uncertainty, not only literally true sentences. Respectful communication can be direct while protecting unrelated confidential information.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Ari promised a draft by 14:00. It is 14:20; the outline exists but the required final paragraph does not. Ari can finish by 15:00 and send then. The recipient needs it for a 15:30 meeting and asks “Is the complete draft ready?” An unrelated colleague’s private problem is not needed to explain the status.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Answer the exact question, acknowledge lateness, give a feasible next step and leave the recipient free to choose another arrangement. Do not invent a cause or completed work.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person sent a file but has not checked that the attachment opens. Asked “can you use it now?”, may they answer “yes, definitely”?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: “No. I missed 14:00; the final paragraph is unfinished. I can send the complete draft by 15:00. Does that still work for your meeting?” is suitable. Later fiction: recipient asks for the outline now and final at 15:00; that is a new agreed arrangement, not a completed delivery. Partial: accurate estimate but evade the direct question. Incorrect: say “nearly ready” to imply complete or expose private details.
criteria: The direct question is answered accurately
Relevant uncertainty and omission are visible
Privacy and a feasible correction are preserved

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Say it was sent and usability is unconfirmed; check through a suitable route. Sending and usable receipt are different facts.
